contact: EBRPD Reservations, (888) 327-2757 option 2, Monday-Friday 9am-4pm Pacific, closed weekends and holidays. Also in person, walk-in, at District HQ, 2950 Peralta Oaks Ct., Oakland. For hearing impairments use the Telecommunications Relay Service at 711; callers in Canada use 510-544-2707. EBRPD warns that Reservations often runs very high call volumes with extended waits, and that a busy signal means the call centre is at its maximum and you should try again later -- so the phone channel can refuse you outright, which matters most on a block-release morning when it is the only channel open.
not_accepted: reservations@ebparks.org is published as the reservations email address and accepts NO reservations -- general inquiries only. Emailing it and waiting is not a booking. A RESERVATION OBTAINED FROM ANYONE BUT EBRPD IS VOID: reservations are for personal use only, and any resale, transfer, for-profit use or membership arrangement not approved in advance by a Special Event permit is cancelled immediately, without notice, refund or reimbursement. EBRPD states there are currently NO approved third-party vendors, so every third-party booking is void. Public advertising of a reservation, including on social media, Meetup or Eventbrite, needs a special event permit on file. THE SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT HAS A LEAD TIME AND IT IS LONG: Morgan Territory's listing says a publicly advertised event needs a valid special event permit on file AT LEAST 60 DAYS before the event date. Every other surface says only that the permit is needed. Sixty days is longer than the entire booking horizon for a backpack site, whose reservations close 48 hours out -- so a group that books a site and then posts about it has almost certainly missed the permit deadline.
change_cancel: Changes and cancellations are NOT accepted by email, even though reservations@ebparks.org is published -- the same address that accepts no bookings accepts no cancellations. Call (888) 327-2757 option 2, or 510-544-2707 from Canada, Mon-Fri 9am-4pm Pacific. EBRPD publishes a Seasonal and Site Closure List (PDF) and asks that it be reviewed BEFORE calling to inquire. This project has not read it, and it is the document most likely to settle whether Anthony Chabot is open between November and April.
release_mechanics: On a reservation opening date: phone only from 9am, no walk-ins, phones closed 12-1pm, and a maximum of two reservations per call. A party needing three sites needs a second call, at the moment the line is busiest.

method: Online at reserveamerica.com (search the park name), or by phone through EBRPD Reservations. EXCEPT ADA CAMPSITES, WHICH ARE PHONE ONLY -- an accessible site cannot be booked through the same online checkout that sells every other family site, so a camper who needs one must call during office hours and cannot secure it at the moment inventory opens online.
lead_time: Online booking opens 12 weeks ahead and closes 48 hours before arrival. EBRPD's reservations page states the minimum as 2 business days rather than 48 hours; over a weekend those differ, and which applies may follow the channel -- 48 hours online, 2 business days by phone -- but that reading is not stated by either source.
change_cancel: A family campsite reservation CAN be cancelled online, but CANNOT be changed online -- any change means calling Reservations during office hours. Booking a different date is therefore not self-service. THE FULL FAMILY SCHEDULE, FROM DEL VALLE'S FACILITY AND NOT FOUND BEFORE. It covers 'Standard, RV, and Hike-in Tent Sites'. Cancel online or by phone. The $8.00 reservation fee is never refundable, and an $8.00 cancellation OR change fee applies on top. Changes must be made BY PHONE, no later than 4:00 PM Pacific, at least 2 business days before arrival. AND THE REFUND IS PRORATED BY NIGHT, which nothing else in this table does: any nights falling within 48 hours of the cancellation request are non-refundable, and only the nights outside that window may be refunded, less fees. So cancelling a four-night stay the day before loses the first night and refunds the rest -- a different shape entirely from the group tiers, which refund a percentage of the whole booking.
release_mechanics: Family campsites, including tent sites, full-hookup sites and cabins, are released on a rolling 12-week window -- unlike group and backpack sites, which go in six-month blocks.

method: Phone only, through EBRPD Reservations. Backpack campsites are NOT bookable online -- reserveamerica.com does not sell them. AFTER BOOKING: an information letter WITH THE PARKING PASSES is emailed 'approximately one week' before the reservation begins, and the passes must be printed and displayed on the dash. That is a third figure for the same letter -- the group row says 5-7 days, Arroyo Flats' own page says 5-10, and this says about a week. All three are EBRPD's.
lead_time: At least 48 hours before arrival, by phone.
change_cancel: DEADLINE AND PRICE, both stated: cancel or change at least TWO DAYS before the arrival date, by phone, calling up to 4pm. An $8 CANCELLATION FEE and a separate $8 NON-REFUNDABLE CHANGE FEE apply, and the $8 reservation fee paid at booking is never refunded -- so a cancelled backpack trip costs $16 before any nightly rate. Changes cannot be made online. NO REFUNDS for inclement weather of any kind (heat, wind, rain), for stricter fire restrictions, or for water quality issues: the three things most likely to stop the trip are the three EBRPD will not refund. ReserveAmerica sells optional Sensible Weather insurance; the Park District states it is not affiliated with it.
release_mechanics: TWO SIX-MONTH BLOCK RELEASES, not a rolling window. Arrival dates July-December 2026 are open now; January-June 2027 opens for reservation in December 2026. So a date is unbookable until its block opens, however far ahead you plan, and the whole half-year competes on one morning.
horizon: Arrival dates through December 2026; January-June 2027 opens December 2026.

method: Phone only, through EBRPD Reservations. Group campsites are NOT bookable online. Availability can be viewed on ReserveAmerica, but the booking itself is by phone. AFTER BOOKING, AND BEFORE ARRIVAL, AN INFORMATION LETTER IS EMAILED: EBRPD says a cabin, group, backpack or equestrian reservation gets an additional information letter 5-7 days before the stay starts. It is not optional reading -- at Arroyo Flats it carries the combination for the group site's locked gate, and that site's own page says 5-10 days rather than 5-7. A party that has not received it may be unable to get in.
lead_time: At least 3 days before arrival, by phone. EBRPD's own pages say '3 business days' and the booking system says '3 days'; over a weekend those differ. REINHARDT REDWOOD'S BOOKING RULES GIVE IT IN HOURS -- 'at least 72 hours (3 days) prior to your arrival date' -- which is the first unambiguous statement of what the booking system means, and it means calendar hours, not business days. So the booking system's floor is 72 hours and EBRPD's prose floor is three business days; a Friday call for a Monday arrival clears the first and fails the second.
change_cancel: Changes and cancellations by phone only. Not cancellable online. Equestrian reservations are handled the same way. THE REFUND SCHEDULE IS TIERED, and this is the first place this project has it: 14 or more days ahead, 90% of site use fees refundable; 13 to 3 days, 50%; UNDER 3 DAYS, NO REFUND of site fees. The damage deposit is fully refundable at every tier. CHANGES: none at all under 3 days; 3 or more days ahead a change costs an $8.00 non-refundable reservation service fee plus any extra nights, or a refund less the $8.00 change fee. NO REFUNDS for inclement weather of any kind, for stricter fire restrictions, or for water quality issues -- the three things most likely to stop the trip, the same terms the backpack row carries. ReserveAmerica sells optional Sensible Weather insurance and the District states it is not affiliated with it. THE DAMAGE DEPOSIT IS ONE NIGHT'S SITE FEE per reservation, refundable if there are no violations and the site is left needing only regular servicing. A group is held financially responsible for damage, for excessive staff intervention to enforce park rules, and for violating any term of the contract. Credit-card refunds take 14-21 days after the campout; cheque, cash or money order refunds are issued as a cheque and take 4-6 WEEKS.
release_mechanics: TWO SIX-MONTH BLOCK RELEASES, not a rolling window. Arrival dates July-December 2026 are open now; January-June 2027 opens for reservation in December 2026. So a date is unbookable until its block opens, however far ahead you plan, and the whole half-year competes on one morning.
horizon: Arrival dates through December 2026; January-June 2027 opens December 2026.

lead_time: THIS PARK ASKS FOR MORE TIME THAN THE DISTRICT DOES, and it is the first booking mechanic here that is not agency-wide. Stated on Dairy Glen's listing: 'Reservations must be completed and paid in full 5 working days prior to your arrival date or 3 days prior if picking up parking passes/permits.' The District's group row says at least 3 days (its own pages say 3 BUSINESS days, its booking system says 3 days). So five working days is the figure to plan on, and the three-day version appears here only as the shorter deadline for a party collecting passes -- read the wrong way round, it looks like the District figure and is not. NOTE ALSO 'PAID IN FULL', which nothing else in this table says: holding a slot without payment is not a reservation under this wording. SCOPE IS A JUDGEMENT AND IS RECORDED AS ONE. This sentence was read on one campsite page, Dairy Glen's. It is stored at park scope because the four other EBRPD group and backpack listings read for this project -- Star Mine, Stewartville, Briones and Round Valley -- do not carry it, so it is not District-wide boilerplate that simply went unnoticed. It could still be narrower than a park: it may belong to this one site. If a second Coyote Hills camp turns up without it, this row should move to site scope, which this schema does not yet have. THE SCOPE ARGUMENT IS WEAKER TODAY THAN IT WAS YESTERDAY. It rested on no other EBRPD LISTING carrying a five-day figure, which is still true. But Briones' 2026/6 map brochure says its group camps 'must be reserved at least five business days in advance' -- a different document type, a different park, and the same departure from the District's three. That thread, briones-group-lead-time, was closed at three on weight of agreement, and the brochure's five was left unexplained. Two parks now publish a five-day requirement the District does not. That is not enough to move this row to agency scope, because the District's own surfaces still say three and the booking system is what refuses a late call -- but 'this sentence appears at one park' is no longer the same argument as 'a longer deadline appears at one park'.

method: PHONE ONLY. 'Cabin reservations can be made over the phone between 72 hours and 12 weeks in advance of your arrival date.' Cabins are not sold online even at the three parks whose family campsites are -- the alert banner naming online booking says 'Tent or RV campsite', and a cabin is neither.
lead_time: Between 72 hours and 12 weeks before arrival. The far end matches the family campsite window and the near end is the GROUP floor, 72 hours, not the family one of 48 hours. A cabin is booked on the family calendar and closed on the group clock.
change_cancel: Cancel or change by PHONE only, on the GROUP schedule rather than the family one: 14 or more days ahead, 90% of site use fees refundable; 13 to 3 days, 50%; under 3 days, nothing. No changes at all under 3 days; $8.00 above it. A damage deposit of one night's fee applies, fully refundable, repaid in 14-21 days by card or 4-6 WEEKS by cheque. CABINS COUNT TOWARD THE HOUSEHOLD'S TWO-SITE LIMIT, so a party booking a cabin and two family sites on one date will have one cancelled.
